author: Claude (acting lead)
correction: My original analysis called a code-signing page kill (cs_invalid_page with CS_KILL) the leading candidate. Grok's independent interpretation (reports/sprint-010/shared-shell-return-attempt002-exit-reason-interpretation.json) shows that path does not produce this record, and I verified it in pinned XNU. When cs_invalid_page reports cs_killed, vm_fault creates and installs OS_REASON_CODESIGNING / CODESIGNING_EXIT_REASON_INVALID_PAGE (osfmk/vm/vm_fault.c ~3105-3109). threadsignal(..., set_exitreason=TRUE) names its sender 'exc handler' (bsd/kern/kern_sig.c ~1815-1822). The attempt002 record (OS_REASON_SIGNAL, code 9, kcdata PID 14 and PROCNAME chonk-terminal-darwin) therefore excludes the code-signing page kill.
what_the_record_does_fit: A psignal(SIGKILL) with a NULL reason executed while current_proc() was pid 14. That is either pid 14's own kill/killpg syscall targeting itself, or a kernel path on pid 14's own thread that calls psignal(p, SIGKILL) without a reason.

plausible_in_victim_context.self_kill_syscall: kill(0 | 14 | -14, SIGKILL) from pid 14. No such call exists in app002 before pty-rx.bin creation, but libSystem and dyld initializers were not audited at binary level.
plausible_in_victim_context.memorystatus_dirty_tracking: kern_memorystatus.c ~3611-3616 and ~3721-3726: psignal(p, SIGKILL) when a dirty-state update finds the process marked for termination. These run in the caller's context if the process itself issues the memorystatus_control dirty call. Not shown to happen here.
plausible_in_victim_context.process_policy_resource_terminate: process_policy.c ~723-727: PROC_POLICY_RSRCACT_TERMINATE. Possible from resource-action callbacks; not expected 9 ms into a process's life.

not_matching_this_record.kern_exit.c ~2615-2620: Kills traced children when their tracer exits (runs in the tracer's context).
not_matching_this_record.kern_proc.c ~6712: pid_resume memory-error path (runs in the resuming caller's context).
not_matching_this_record.osfmk task_identity_token_try_sigkill: A caller holding a task identity token (runs in that caller's context).
not_matching_this_record.kern_guarded.c ~1304 vnguard: Default policy flags have no SIGKILL, and no vnguard boot argument is set.
not_matching_this_record.kern_proc.c ~3868/3896 csops MARKINVALID: Only in the caller's context. No userspace caller was found in the PureDarwin sources searched; not excluded at binary level.

effect_on_candidate_003: The revision006 serialized-launch test (B1) stays a valid behaviour test whatever the mechanism. Spawn-time CS flags (D2) remain a harmless live record. Grok notes cs_at_exit is expected to be ESRCH on this XNU.
